decisions.context: Millions of documents arrive daily, with volume that varies through the year. The brief does not require immediate predictions for each incoming document.
decisions.rationale: Batch scoring fits the stated scale and shared consumption model; no per-document response-time requirement is given. Sources including “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline” and “System Architectures for Personalization and Recommendation” describe scheduled scoring.
consequences: Consumers read results from shared storage or analytics systems.
Results reflect the most recent completed scoring run.

decisions.context: Classification demand varies strongly over the year, so capacity needs to respond to workload changes. The brief does not specify a hosting platform or latency target.

alternatives.label: Scale-to-zero serving
cons: may not suit scheduled batch capacity

decisions.rationale: Elastic scaling directly addresses seasonal workload variation and large processing volumes. “Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline” and “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture” support scaling compute with demand.
consequences: Scaling behavior and limits need operational configuration.

decisions.context: Operators need visibility when classification quality drifts. Monitoring can combine practices: this design-space dimension has zero exclusivity, and the checked point warns that it permits only one value per dimension.

alternatives.label: Input and feature-drift monitoring
cons: drift alone does not measure quality

decisions.rationale: Choose drift monitoring to give operators visibility into changing inputs, and combine it with prediction-quality monitoring when labels become available. “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture” and “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” support drift monitoring; “Machine Learning Monitoring: What It Is, and What We Are Missing” supports quality monitoring.
consequences: Monitor input and feature changes in production.
Assess prediction quality when ground-truth labels arrive.
The checked design point flags the combined monitoring values as a same-dimension warning.

decisions.context: Several teams consume classification results, so the system needs a defined way to expose predictions. The brief does not specify how those teams integrate.
decisions.rationale: A REST interface is a broadly supported option for exposing model predictions to multiple application consumers. “How to power up your product by machine learning with python microservice” and “Three Levels of ML Software” document this approach.
consequences: Service ownership and access patterns remain to be specified.

uncovered: Data ingestion mechanism and source integration; the design-space relation says workflow coordination requires this decision first.
Result schema, storage retention, and access control for the consuming teams.
Ground-truth label collection and its delay, needed to define prediction-quality monitoring.
Classification error costs, acceptance thresholds, and human review policy.
Deployment platform, availability targets, and batch schedule.
